sources.title: When should I use web search, extended thinking, and research?

folds.text: Claude has three ways to dig deeper, and each suits a different job. Picking the right one saves time and usage.
**Web search** is for quick, factual questions: the weather, a company, recent news. Claude looks it up and answers.
**Extended thinking** is for complex reasoning that needs no fresh web info, like debugging code or improving an algorithm.

**Research** is for big questions. Claude runs several searches that build on each other and writes an in-depth answer. It takes longer and can use your limits faster, so save it for jobs that need it.

folds.question: You want a detailed comparison of several phone plans from many sources. What fits best?
folds.why: A broad question across many sources is a research job. Web search suits a quick, factual question.
